Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 43 s. 2022 May 24, 2022 HON. JANREY G. GAVINA City Vice Mayor City of Panabo Province of Davao del Norte Dear Vice-Mayor Gavi na. This pertains to your letter dated 5 January 2022 requesting for intercession on the adverse situation involving the executive and legislative actions concerning the hiring of casual/Job Order employees. Below are the submitted issues and the corresponding discussions in response thereto: 1. "Is the Vice Mayor's authority to hire employees/job order in the Sanggunian extends to his authority to sign the Memorandum of Agreement between the Sanggunian and the job order? If so, does this not contradict Section 77 of LGC?" 2. "Is the City mayor's request for an authority to enter into and sign a Memorandum of Agreement between him and Sanggunian employees an encroachment on duties and authority of the City Vice Mayor?" 3. "Can an Appropriation Ordinance Authorizing the Annual Budget of the City enough to support as basis for authority to hire individual/s as job order/contract of The issue concerning the first and second queries was explained in DILG Opinion No. 34, s. 2014 where the Department modified previous opinions on the matter in view of the Supreme Court's pronouncement in the case of Vicencio vs. Villar, et. al.l It was held that under Section. 456(2) of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991 " (LGC), there is no inherent authority on the part of the city vice-mayor to enter into contracts on behalf of the local government unit, unlike that provided for the city mayor. In that case, the Supreme Court nevertheless gave an instance in the same case where the vice-mayor may enter into a contract on behalf of the city, viz: "Thus, the authority of the vice-mayor to enter into contracts on behalf of 1 G.R. No. 182969, 03 July 2012. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

the city was strictly circumscribed by the ordinance granting it. Ordinance No. 15-2003 specifically authorized Vice Mayor Yambao to enter contracts for consultancy services. As this is not a power or duty given under the law to the office of the vice-mayor, Ordinance No. 15-2003 cannot be construed as a 'continuing authority' for any person who enters the Office of the Vice-Mayor to enter into subsequent, albeit similar, contracts. " Verily, said jurisprudence clarified that hiring of employees under the Job Order contractual status does not fall within the purview of the vice-mayor's appointing authority under Section 456(2) of the Local Government Code which is limited to positions subject to civil service law. We, therefore, reiterate, the modification effected by DILG Opinion No. 34, s. 2014 which state as follows: "In view of the recent ruling of the Supreme Court in Villar case, the Department's opinion as embodied in DILG. Opinion Nos. 23-2005, 17- 2010 and 2011 are hereby modified. As a general rule, all contracts of services and job orders shall be entered into by the local chief executive of the local government unit, except in cases where there is an ordinance passed by the sanggunian specifically authorizing the vice-mayor or vice- governor to enter into contracts on behalf of the local govemment unit. " For the third query, we submit an affirmative view as to the budgetary aspect relative to the hiring. It is to be reminded, however, that other bases may be required by other pertinent laws relative to accounting and auditing regulations. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARL NGAN re ryfor Local Govern ent Unde LLLS/RPB/LRALLD/kvb Copy-tur_njsbgg: MAYOR JOSE E.
